title: GTA6 Named Among TGA 2026 GOTY Front-Runners by Polygon
description: Polygon ranks Grand Theft Auto 6 and Resident Evil Requiem as top contenders for Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2026. Read the latest analysis.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## TGA 2026: GTA6 and Resident Evil Requiem Lead GOTY Contenders

As the gaming landscape progresses through 2026, major media outlets are already looking ahead to the industry's biggest night: The Game Awards. In a recent feature by prominent gaming publication Polygon, the outlet ranked the leading contenders for Game of the Year (GOTY) at TGA 2026, placing Grand Theft Auto 6 alongside Resident Evil Requiem as top front-runners for the ultimate accolade.

### A Competitive Year for Gaming

The race for Game of the Year is always fiercely contested, but 2026 is shaping up to be a monumental year for blockbuster releases. Polygon's early ranking highlights how major titles are positioning themselves for award season. Among the contenders, GTA6 has captured the attention of critics and fans alike, naturally placing it at the forefront of these early GOTY discussions. Joining it in the spotlight is Resident Evil Requiem, which has also turned heads with its critical reception and strong presence among gamers.

### Industry Analysis and Early Predictions

While the official award ceremony is still months away, early rankings by outlets like Polygon set the tone for the annual GOTY debate. Industry analysts note that titles of this scale carry massive expectations, not just in terms of commercial success, but in pushing technical boundaries and delivering unforgettable experiences. The inclusion of GTA6 in these early conversations underscores the monumental anticipation surrounding the title.

### Editor's Take

Seeing GTA6 position itself among the top contenders for TGA 2026 by Polygon comes as no surprise given its massive footprint in the industry. Whether it ultimately takes home the trophy remains to be seen, but the 2026 GOTY race is already shaping up to be one for the history books.
